new_or_replaced_slides.title: What a test can’t tell us today
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: A software test checks the run today; only mature labels can check the prediction.
bullets: Today: tests show the job runs, inputs are valid, and scores are saved.
Not today: whether Ana’s 0.70 is right. Her 30-day outcome is unknown.
Later: link labels to the scores, then measure precision and recall.
Fixed model: same inputs, same score. The uncertainty is predictive.
new_or_replaced_slides.example: Ana / C042: scored 0.70 today. Only churn labels, available after the 30-day window, show whether she left.
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: The bank need not wait 30 days to catch an incompatible input.

new_or_replaced_slides.title: How do predictions reach the business?
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: It depends on when the decision needs them: offline (batch) or real-time, synchronously or asynchronously.
bullets: Offline: historical data in bulk; results are read later.
Real-time: current context plus history, per request.
Location: central, embedded or edge is a separate axis.
Ask first: does the decision need real-time? (Nazir, I12)
new_or_replaced_slides.example: Ana's risk is needed only before the monthly campaign: a central batch suffices. Edge adds rollout cost, no benefit.
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: Churn needs none of the online paths: monthly, central, batch.
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Kalinowski, §13.3, Fig. 13.2–13.4; supporting Ch. 12 · Nazir et al., §4.3 (I12)

new_or_replaced_slides.title: Batch path: Ana's score on day D0
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: A complete, validated batch must be published before the campaign deadline.
bullets: Snapshot: define population, cutoff, and source freshness.
Validate: reject incompatible inputs before scoring.
Reconcile: account for written, rejected, withheld records.
Publish: expose the validated batch under a consumer contract.
new_or_replaced_slides.example: Ana's 0.70 is stored with M1, D0 and the feature version; her 30-day outcome is still unknown on D0.
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: Saving batch scores at scale is a reported challenge (Nazir, I6).
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Bass, §14.1.4 · Kalinowski, §13.3, Fig. 13.2 · Nazir et al., §3.2 (I6)

new_or_replaced_slides.title: Online serving: the fraud contrast
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: Same domain, different timing needs. A comparison, not a new part of the churn system.
bullets: Model time: smaller models, leaner code, GPU/TPU at a cost.
System time: fast input lookup; precomputed, cached scores.
Inputs: the back-end usually fetches features the caller lacks.
Async: idempotent consumers, lag and failed-message handling.
new_or_replaced_slides.example: Fraud blocking is synchronous, fraud alerts asynchronous. Churn stays batch; CRM can read Ana's cached score.
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: A fast model does not guarantee a fast end-to-end service.
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Kalinowski, §13.3–13.4, Fig. 13.3–13.4 · Fraud and CRM cases are teaching comparisons

new_or_replaced_slides.title: Package the whole compatible set
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: A deployable release contains more than the learned model file.
bullets: Model artifact: the learned parameters and required format.
Runtime: dependencies, preparation code, environment.
Contract: feature meaning, types, missingness, cutoff.
Configuration: scoring population and execution settings.
new_or_replaced_slides.example: M1 ships with the exact feature meaning it was trained on, such as the 7-day login count used to score C042.
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: Smoke-test in the serving environment before exposure (Breck, infra. 6).
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Bass, §14.1.4 · Kalinowski, §13.3 · Nazir et al., §4.1, Table 12 · Breck et al., infra. test 6

new_or_replaced_slides.title: Shadow deployment: observe without acting
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: A candidate scores real inputs while the approved model remains the action source.
bullets: Run in parallel against the same production snapshot.
Record identity: label M1 and M2 outputs explicitly.
Compare operational behavior and score differences first.
Wait for labels to compare 30-day churn quality.
new_or_replaced_slides.example: Only M1's 0.70 for Ana is eligible for campaign use; M2's shadow score is logged and cannot create a second offer.
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: Shadow checks observation, not the business effect of acting on the candidate.
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Bass, §14.1.4 · Bank teaching application of the group release plan

new_or_replaced_slides.title: Release strategies: what each proves
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: Shadow, canary and A/B tests answer different questions on different clocks.
bullets: Canary: limit exposure; set stop rules and a rollback.
A/B test: state what changes: model, policy or offer.
Confounding: changing model and offer together hides both.
Labels: D0 success cannot prove 30-day quality.
new_or_replaced_slides.example: Ask 'does M2 rank churn risk better than M1?' separately from 'does offer B retain more customers than offer A?'
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: A canary controls risk; it is not automatically an experiment.
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Breck et al., infra. tests 6–7 · Bank teaching application

new_or_replaced_slides.title: Release plan: shadow, canary, rollback
new_or_replaced_slides.lead: Proposed decision: evidence arrives on two clocks, so exposure grows in steps.
bullets: Decision: central monthly batch; shadow M2, then canary.
Trade-off: one or two extra cycles before M2 is fully used.
Rollback: reuse the last validated M1 batch only while it remains eligible and fresh.
Record: link model, features, config and approval (Matheus).
new_or_replaced_slides.example: The first scoring run worked. What evidence tells us the system stays reliable as data and customers change?
new_or_replaced_slides.takeaway: Exposure grows only as evidence arrives.
new_or_replaced_slides.source: Breck et al., infra. tests 6–7 · Nazir et al., §4.1 · Proposed bank release design
new_or_replaced_slides.extra: The staged rollout is a proposed teaching design. Reusing an older batch requires valid population, feature meaning, freshness and campaign eligibility. Otherwise pause use or produce a new validated batch with the compatible approved model. Model rollback does not repair the later CRM input fault.
